Working with cost variables

Source: vignettes/articles/costs.Rmd
costs.Rmd

usRds has four functions that extract amounts from Medicare claims, and two that adjust them. The claim files carry several different amounts for the same service, and they answer different questions. This page says what each amount is, which ones to use for common questions, and where the current functions fall short.

All column descriptions come from Appendix B of the 2025 USRDS Researcher’s Guide, and the cautions from Section 5 of the Guide (“Medicare Claims”). Check them against the Guide for the release you are using: earlier releases may differ.

The four extractors

Function Claims One row per Years in usRds
get_IN_CLM_costs() Institutional: inpatient, outpatient, skilled nursing, home health, hospice claim 2006–2021, and inpatient 2022 Q1
get_IN_REV_costs() Institutional revenue center line 2006–2021, and inpatient 2022 Q1
get_PS_CLM_costs() Physician/Supplier and durable medical equipment (DME) claim 2013–2021
get_PS_REV_costs() Physician/Supplier and DME claim line 2006–2021

The year ranges are those of the package’s internal file tables, not of the data. Files for later years exist (Appendix B 2025 describes 2023 files), but the package does not read them yet.

What each amount is

Kinds of amount. A submitted charge is what the provider billed. An allowed amount is what Medicare’s fee schedule allows for the service. A payment is money actually paid, by Medicare or by someone else. These can differ a great deal: submitted charges can be several times the payment.

Institutional claims: get_IN_CLM_costs()

Column Appendix B description Kind
CLM_TOT Total charges submitted charge
CLM_AMT Medicare payments payment (Medicare)

For inpatient claims, the Guide notes that Medicare’s cost also includes pass-through payments (for example indirect medical education, capital, and kidney acquisition for transplant), found by multiplying PER_DIEM by the covered days CVR_DCNT. usRds does not read these columns yet (#65), so CLM_AMT alone understates inpatient cost.

Institutional revenue lines: get_IN_REV_costs()

Column Appendix B description Kind
REV_CH Revenue center total charge submitted charge
REVPMT Revenue center payment amount payment (Medicare)

Revenue lines break a claim’s charges down by type of service. Two cautions from the Guide:

  • Revenue center code 0001 holds the sum of the claim’s other lines, so adding up REV_CH over every line counts charges twice. This function does not return the revenue center code, so you cannot drop those lines yet (#112).
  • REVPMT exists for outpatient claims from 2001. Summed over a claim, it does not always match the claim’s CLM_AMT; the Guide found outpatient REVPMT totals about 3% higher.

The function also returns no CLM_THRU, so its output cannot go straight into prorate_costs_by_day() (#66).

Physician/Supplier claims: get_PS_CLM_costs()

Column Appendix B description Kind
CLM_PMT_AMT Amount paid by Medicare payment (Medicare)
NCH_CLM_PRVDR_PMT_AMT Total payments to the provider payment
NCH_CLM_BENE_PMT_AMT Total payment to beneficiary payment (to the patient)
CARR_CLM_PRMRY_PYR_PD_AMT Amount paid by primary payer (not Medicare) payment (other payer)
NCH_CARR_SBMT_CHRG_AMT Submitted charge amount submitted charge
NCH_CARR_ALOW_CHRG_AMT Allowed charge amount allowed amount
CARR_CLM_CASH_DDCTBL_APPLY_AMT Cash deductible amount deductible

“Payment to beneficiary” is money Medicare paid to the patient, not money the patient paid.

Physician/Supplier lines: get_PS_REV_costs()

Column Appendix B description Kind
SBMTCH Submitted charges submitted charge
ALOWCH Allowed charges allowed amount
PMTAMT Claim payment amount (for the line) payment

Appendix B also lists line amounts for the beneficiary’s payment, deductible and coinsurance, and the primary payer’s payment. usRds does not read them yet (#65).

Which amount to use

  • What Medicare spent: CLM_AMT (institutional) and CLM_PMT_AMT (Physician/Supplier), from the claim-level functions. This is what is usually meant by Medicare cost.
  • Spending by type of service: the line-level functions, with the cautions above.
  • What the service would cost at Medicare rates: allowed amounts (NCH_CARR_ALOW_CHRG_AMT, ALOWCH), Physician/Supplier only.
  • Charges: rarely the right measure of cost, because they reflect providers’ list prices rather than what anyone paid.

Two more points:

  1. Don’t add claim totals and line amounts for the same claims. The line amounts are a breakdown of the claim totals, so adding both counts the same money twice. This applies whatever you measure.

  2. Choose the payer restriction to fit the question. When Medicare is a secondary payer, or the patient is in a Medicare Advantage plan, the claims do not show the full cost of care. So the Annual Data Report’s per-person-per-year costs count only fee-for-service claims, during time when Medicare was the primary payer (2017 ADR, Volume 2, ESRD Analytical Methods, Chapter 9). Use the same restriction when you need complete costs per person. A total of what Medicare spent is a different question, and may rightly include Medicare’s payments as a secondary payer.

    verify_medicare_primary() checks Medicare-primary coverage on one index date and the lookback before it. It does not check coverage over the whole follow-up, so periods of coverage during follow-up need their own check (#23).

Adjusting and spreading amounts

adjust_costs_for_inflation() adds an _ADJUSTED copy of each amount, converted to the dollars of a month and year you choose with the medical care consumer price index (BLS series CUUR0000SAM, 2006–2025 in the package). Each claim uses the index for the month of its CLM_FROM.

prorate_costs_by_day() spreads each claim’s amounts evenly over the days from CLM_FROM to CLM_THRU, one row per day, so costs can be counted by day, month or follow-up period. Claims with a missing or reversed date are left out, with a warning.

The two work in either order. Here they are on two made-up claims:

library(usRds)

claims <- data.frame(
  USRDS_ID = c(1, 2),
  CLM_FROM = as.Date(c("2010-06-01", "2015-12-01")),
  CLM_THRU = as.Date(c("2010-06-03", "2015-12-01")),
  CLM_PMT_AMT = c(300, 100)
)

adjusted <- adjust_costs_for_inflation(
  claims,
  baseline_month = "December",
  baseline_year = 2015
)
adjusted
#>   USRDS_ID   CLM_FROM   CLM_THRU CLM_PMT_AMT CLM_PMT_AMT_ADJUSTED
#> 1        1 2010-06-01 2010-06-03         300             348.5882
#> 2        2 2015-12-01 2015-12-01         100             100.0000

daily <- prorate_costs_by_day(adjusted)
daily
#>   USRDS_ID   CLM_FROM   CLM_THRU service_date CLM_PMT_AMT_PRORATED
#> 1        1 2010-06-01 2010-06-03   2010-06-01                  100
#> 2        1 2010-06-01 2010-06-03   2010-06-02                  100
#> 3        1 2010-06-01 2010-06-03   2010-06-03                  100
#> 4        2 2015-12-01 2015-12-01   2015-12-01                  100
#>   CLM_PMT_AMT_ADJUSTED_PRORATED
#> 1                      116.1961
#> 2                      116.1961
#> 3                      116.1961
#> 4                      100.0000

Totals are kept by proration:

all.equal(
  sum(daily$CLM_PMT_AMT_ADJUSTED_PRORATED),
  sum(adjusted$CLM_PMT_AMT_ADJUSTED)
)
#> [1] TRUE

Known gaps

  • Some amounts are not read: inpatient pass-through payments, the institutional primary-payer and deductible amounts (from the 2015 files), and the Physician/Supplier line beneficiary amounts (#65).
  • get_IN_REV_costs() returns neither the revenue center code (#112) nor CLM_THRU (#66).
  • get_PS_CLM_costs(remove_missing_values = ) has no effect: claims with a missing payment are kept (#54). get_PS_REV_costs() drops lines with a missing PMTAMT unless remove_missing_values = FALSE.
  • DME claims have claim type code E, which shows as NA in HCFASAF (#27).
  • The package’s file tables stop at 2021 (2022 Q1 for inpatient claims).
